candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16: identify medication interactions, indications, and monitor/evaluate medication therapy
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — drug interaction / aprepitant and dexamethasone
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the clinically significant aprepitant-dexamethasone interaction and the labeled recommendation to reduce oral dexamethasone by approximately 50% during the standard 3-day aprepitant regimen.

options.A: Reduce the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50%
options.B: Increase the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50%
options.C: Make no dexamethasone adjustment because aprepitant does not affect its exposure
options.D: Discontinue dexamethasone solely because it is contraindicated with aprepitant

candidate.rationale: Current aprepitant labeling states that the 3-day aprepitant regimen increases dexamethasone exposure and recommends reducing the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50%. The label does not recommend increasing the dose, leaving it unchanged in this regimen, or treating dexamethasone as contraindicated. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: During the standard 3-day aprepitant regimen, aprepitant increases dexamethasone exposure and the label recommends an approximately 50% reduction in oral dexamethasone dose.
candidate.source_locator: §2.1 Prevention of Chemotherapy Induced Nausea and Vomiting, dosing tables/footnotes: 50% dexamethasone dosage reduction recommended to account for interaction with aprepitant; §7.1 Table 10, Dexamethasone: increased dexamethasone exposure; 3-day aprepitant regimen — reduce oral dexamethasone by approximately 50%
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: An adult client is prescribed the standard 3-day oral aprepitant regimen for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting prevention together with oral dexamethasone. Which dexamethasone adjustment is expected because of the aprepitant interaction?
